scenes.headline: How old geometry keeps fast 3D models honest
scenes.sub: Loop closure, gravity and edges, bolted onto feed-forward networks
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Halwa! Fast 3D models guess a scene in seconds. This week's papers bolt an older idea onto them.

scenes.text: A network guesses poses and depth roughly. A classical constraint, a revisited place, the direction of gravity, an image edge, turns the guess into geometry that holds.
scenes.mark: turns the guess into geometry that holds
scenes.say: The guess is rough. A revisited place, gravity, or an image edge turns it into geometry that holds.

scenes.title: Closing the loop on a streaming model

steps.say: A streaming model reads the video window by window and outputs poses. Small errors pile up, so the path drifts.
Place recognition notices when a new frame looks like an old one.
New and matched old frames go through the same model together, so their relative pose comes out in one frame.
A pose graph pulls the whole path into line, solving only rotation and translation, because the backbone already keeps its scale.

scenes.title: Mean trajectory error on VBR
scenes.note: seven Rome loops, 2.31 km on average
scenes.say: On long loops through Rome, average error falls from about thirty-six metres to eleven. Less drift, not none.

left.title: Camera frame
items: The floor tilts with the first photo
Two submaps differ by seven numbers
left.say: Most models predict points in the first camera's frame, so the floor tilts with that photo.

right.title: Gravity frame
items: Only scale, shift and one turn
right.say: Predict them upright, and two pieces of a map differ only by scale, a shift and one turn about the vertical.

scenes.title: Bundle adjustment without tracks
scenes.say: The third trick refines poses without matching points.

items.text: Find the edges in every photo
items.say: Find the edges in every photo.

items.text: Project them into the other views
items.say: Project them into the other views with the predicted depth.

items.text: Measure the distance to an edge
items.say: A distance map says how far each landed from a real edge.
Then nudge poses, focal length and depth until they line up.

steps.say: With the network's first guess, edges from another view, in red, sit beside the white ones.
After refinement they lie on top.

scenes.text: The network supplies a fast guess. A loop, gravity or an edge supplies the constraint that makes it hold.
scenes.mark: the constraint that makes it hold
scenes.say: The network supplies a fast guess. An old constraint makes it hold.

recap: Loop closure pulls a drifting path back
Upright frames leave one rotation to solve
Edge alignment refines poses without tracks
scenes.say: Close the loop, keep gravity up, and let edges finish the job.
